items.issue: Hermant, Kiersnowski & Bellanger (2025, Stanford Geothermal Workshop, Fig. 2 & Fig. 9B) document 150-400 m positional offsets between USGS Quaternary fault traces and 3DEP LiDAR scarp breaks. When a scarp detector fires along a known fault and only the 1-px catalogue spine is masked (~labels), the unmasked 100-200 m flank survives as a dense band of dots (5,355 dots = 8.91% of the 0.2477 file sit at d_cat = 100 m; 8,769 dots = 14.60% sit at d_cat <= 200 m). On our non-leaky OOF detector B_oof (seeds 130-139), those d_cat = 100 m dots have hit efficiency 0.0034 (15x below break-even 0.0521).
items.action: Validated H27-4 on B_oof (+0.0022 solo at 100 m, +0.0141 stacked with T-v2 in 4/4 folds) and shipped Tertiary Slot 3 candidate (d466b251f309, 55,992 px).

items.issue: Berkowitz et al. (2000) give ensemble-average connectivity estimates ('rather than particular realizations'); they do not state that one segment decides whether two particular faults join.
items.action: The per-gap argument here rests on the graph analysis and the holdout, not on the paper alone.

items.issue: The raster catalogue has 3,199 8-connected systems (median 1.27 km). In Session 2 we cross-referenced against the 1,179 NBMG INGENIOUS Qfaults vector polylines (qfaults_v2_in_footprint.json, 99.97% match within 200 m) and ran a three-tier holdout (seeds 120-129, evidence/vector_topology_validation.json): z>=3 dedup achieves 0.2926 on 8-connected components (5.00x ctrl), 0.1003 on whole NBMG FID multipart polylines (4.92x ctrl, rising to 0.1374 with H27-5a kinematic typing and 0.1783 with H27-5b same-name kinematic typing), and 0.0014 on whole 20-70 km named fault zones (NAME).
items.action: Both component and whole-FID vector holdout gates pass (> m(0.30) = 0.0638); whole-zone holdout confirms 1-4 km links complete segments within and between traces rather than bridging 15-30 km inter-range basins.

items.issue: knowledge/01 and the operating-point model assume |G| ~ 12.63k px. Session 3 re-derived it from the blind spacing-5 lattice alone (whose credit per truth pixel c = 0.37481 is pure geometry, independent of where the truth is) using the SHA-256-authenticated raster: |G| = 12,226 px. The sibling GEMSDOE25 independently derived 12,503 (lattice) and 12,769 (pair).
items.action: Adopt 12,226 px with a stated range of 12.2-12.8k. All Session-3 modelling uses 12,226. This is a refinement, not a contradiction: the three instruments agree within 2.2-4.3%. evidence/live_inversion.json.

items.issue: A habitat tomography of the hidden truth (20 live scores as 20 linear measurements of the truth intensity lambda) is NOT identifiable from the available corpus. Overlapping bases: in-sample R2 = -1.24. Strict 7-cell catalogue-distance partition: R2 = -0.360, leave-one-submission-out score RMSE 0.0715 vs a score spread of 0.0686 (signal ratio 0.96).
items.action: Recorded so no future session re-derives it or - worse - ships an emission chosen by the fitted lambda. The fitted habitat weights (66% of truth in the 100-200 m catalogue ring) are hypothesis-generating ONLY. evidence/live_truth_partition_radial.json.

items.issue: The live-validated retention rule credit(d) = credit_solid * c(d)/c_solid assumes the hidden truth is spread uniformly near the emission. That is exactly right for geometric (Poisson-disk) thinning - it predicts two independent live solid->dotted pairs to -0.1% and +4.0% - but it is biased against TARGETED pruning, because it charges every removed pixel with average credit. The out-of-fold gate measured the H27-4 catalogue-flank pixels directly at 0.0034 credit/px, about 15x below the 0.0521 live break-even.
items.action: Report BOTH models for every candidate (evidence/candidate_model_scores.json): 'geometric' charges uniform-truth retention for all changes, 'hybrid' charges geometric retention for thinning and the measured OOF efficiencies for the targeted steps. Slot 1 vs slot 3 is the live A/B that settles which is right. Neither column is a score.

An earlier draft of the inversion script summed positives over the WHOLE grid and so charged this file 341,742 scored pixels - a 2.3x overstatement that propagated into its implied credit.
